## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d12550d799990a61099dc752c8b4b1d311259013`

### ① Derived judgments

(a) **The walk's input — RIGHT.** `renderBody` computes one span map, calls `stampRefusals(raw, nowMs, spans)`, then `substituteTokens(raw, stampNow(nowMs), spans)`; inside the refusal `now = stampNow(nowMs)` (:1333) is that same string, so `substituteTokens(raw, now, spans).body` at :1409 is byte-identical to what `writeArtefact` POSTs — it sends `rendered.body` unchanged, no footer, no truncation, and reads it back. The reader is H56's own, imported at :810 and never re-defined (pinned structurally at :3965), so the walk sees exactly the two positions and the same hold-out rule. Rendering can neither create nor move a position: a token always renders non-empty, so the first non-blank line is the same line, and no substitution can emit a subscript opener.

(b) **The two exemptions — parity-preserving, one declared asymmetry.** The multi-stamp hold-out is not code at all: it falls out of the imported reader, so it cannot drift from H56. It is not a typing hole — a hand-typed bare stamp beside a declaration is still caught, because the bare walk runs on `maskQuotedStamps`'d text (:1382) where only the declaration is blanked (reproduced). `hit.stamp === now` (:1411) is load-bearing twice: it also exempts this act's own substituted token, which is why ablation leg B crashed rather than reddened. It does open one narrow spelling hole: a declaration typed equal to this act's minute is ACCEPTED at a position while the byte-identical bare stamp is REFUSED `positional` — I reproduced both. Judged acceptable: the bytes are the ones the act-clock token would write, the patrol is silent on both, and the header declares the asymmetry at :98-100. Using it requires knowing the minute exactly, i.e. reading a clock.

(c) **The `quotedValueProblems === 0` gate — safe, but incomplete and mis-described.** The gate at :1408 is body-wide; its comment at :1377-1379 describes a per-VALUE rule. Reproduced: a shape-refused declaration anywhere suppresses the row for a real declared reading standing on the opening line, which the patrol would file. It is not a hole — `renderBody` refuses on any row, so nothing reaches the board — but the caller fixes one thing, re-runs, and is refused again. Same shape in `positionsTaken`, whose key is position-name plus stamp, so two different subscript lines carrying the same stamp collapse to one row. Both safe; both follow-ups, neither blocks.

(d) **The flipped self-test (:3054) — the old assertion was the defect.** It pinned as intended behaviour the exact body the card measured filed twice on live artefacts written by following this file's own prescription. No legitimate use lost: the remedy is the one the card's author already applied by hand, and no artefact was found whose opening line must carry a reading. Bonus fix: the old row passed no `nowMs`, so it judged direction against the wall clock; the replacement passes the fixed clock.

(e) **The header rewrite — claim now true; one prescription still offers the declared token at a position.** The parity sentence at :42-44 is now one-directional (patrol-could-file implies refused-before-the-write) and holds at the body level, including under the (c) gate. The POSITIONAL row (:46-50) and the refusal text (:1396-1398) no longer offer the declared spelling AT the position. But `mixed` still hands back the declared spelling for a bare stamp, and when that stamp sits on a position line carrying two stamps, following the mixed remedy lands on `positional` and then on `positional-declared` — reproduced end to end. Narrow, never accepts a bad body, but it is this file's own "a refusal prescribing a refused remedy" rule: follow-up.

(f) **`now` and the grains — a real over-refusal.** Confirmed from source: `now` is `stampNow(nowMs)`, a MINUTE-grain string; `hit.stamp` is whatever the protocol regex matched, seconds optional. So `hit.stamp === now` compares like with like only at the minute grain. Reproduced: a declaration of this act's OWN clock at the SECONDS grain, at either position, is refused `positional-declared` while the patrol files nothing — the parity claim false the other way round, which is the very thing the exemption exists to prevent. The header hedges to "clock minute" (:94), so no prose is falsified and the direction is the safe one, and the remedy the refusal prints is correct and actionable. But the file pins the seconds grain elsewhere as an accepted grain, and the new battery's own-clock row is minute-only, so nothing pins the seconds arm. Follow-up: compare at minute containment (truncate `hit.stamp` to the minute, or reuse `stampSpan`) and add the seconds row.

(g) **Nothing narrowed beyond the two positions.** The walk iterates only the imported reader's hits. The five moved fixtures are one-liners whose declaration sat on the opening line only because they were one-liners, and each keeps its own subject. Two of them were genuine accepted-form narrowings (a reading of something else on the opening line, minute and seconds grain) and the patrol agrees with both, so the moves are right rather than a batch respelling. The one-liner left in place is the exemption pin. The only narrowing the patrol does not agree with is (f). Battery count checks out: 17 rows in the block at :3933, pinned at 17 at :2983.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is right, and there is no semver level to assign. One file, `scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs`; the root package is `private: true` with no `files[]` and no published package ships `scripts/**`, so nothing user-visible moves. This repo routes such a PR through the label rather than an empty changeset, and "Check Changeset" reads `skipped` on the head, consistent. No `content/docs/releases/` change, no file unrelated to the card. PR is draft, targets `main`, first line is the closing reference, and the change is the whole of route A, so the closing keyword is the right spelling.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **+4 over the +120 budget — accepted, keep the lines.** They are the header's rejected-route paragraph (:106-110); this file keeps every rejected route beside the rule it was rejected for, and moving it into the PR body alone loses it at the point of use. Declared, not taken silently.
- **Ablation leg A against an uncommitted tree, restore destroyed the edits — answered, no rework.** The recorded leg (anchor x1 to x0, blob transition, 7 named failures) is from the committed state, and the evidence face I checked is the diff itself, not the run. Process incident; cost was rework, not a wrong reading.
- **C6 / the owed contract-review record — discharged by this record**, which names this head. The `--pair` exit 4 was report-only and nothing was hung.
- **#19319 (declared token inside a fenced block) — correctly not widened into.** The quote-unaware MIXED refusal is a decision recorded in the file's own header; it stays on #19319.
- **The card's second same-family defect, measured closed by #19280 — accepted as closed.** I re-measured: the placeholder form inside a code span and the split-across-backticks form both clear the opener scan today, so the card's syntax is writable with this tool. One correction to the note: a real-digit declared token QUOTED on the OPENING line takes `positional`, not `mixed`, because `maskQuotedStamps` deliberately does not blank a declaration inside a quoted span; the refusal carries the quoted-span clause, so the behaviour is right, just not the kind the note names.
- **CI on this head, honest reading:** `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Test Core (1/6)` are `in_progress`; every other run is `success` or `skipped`. Not a review defect, and I ran no gate locally — but both must read `success` before the seat flips this ready or queues it.
